title: How IA Marks Affect Your Final IB Grade
summary: IA marks affect final IB grade outcomes through weighting and moderation. Learn the calculation, boundaries, and what students can still control.
body_markdown:
A student opens a grade calculator with two numbers in mind: an IA mark and the grade they hope to see in July. The natural question is simple: how much can the first number change the second?


IA marks affect your final IB grade by contributing a weighted share of your overall subject mark. The exact weighting depends on the subject and level. Your moderated IA mark is scaled to that weighting, combined with your externally assessed components, and then converted into an IB grade from 1-7 using the final subject grade boundaries.


That means a strong IA can create useful breathing room, but it cannot determine the subject grade alone. Equally, a disappointing IA rarely makes a target grade mathematically impossible. What matters is the IA's weighting, any moderation applied by the IB, your examination performance, and the grade boundaries for your examination session.


### The calculation at a glance


Here is the process students and parents need to understand:


- Find the IA's official weighting for the subject and level.
- Convert the raw IA mark into its weighted contribution.
- Remember that teacher-awarded IA marks may be adjusted through moderation.
- Add the weighted IA contribution to the weighted examination components.
- Compare the resulting total with the final subject boundaries.
- Treat historical boundaries as planning evidence, not a promise about a future session.


The distinction between marks and grades matters. A mark records performance on a component. A grade is the final 1-7 outcome after weighted components have been aggregated and the applicable boundaries have been applied.


### Following one student from IA mark to IB grade


Imagine a student called Maya trying to understand her Mathematics IA result. This is a hypothetical example dated November 2026, included only to demonstrate the arithmetic. It is not an official boundary forecast.


Suppose Maya receives 15 out of 20 on an IA worth 20% of the subject result. Her weighted IA contribution would be:

### Why the IA percentage can be misleading


Students often say, “I got 75% on my IA, so I have 75% of my final grade.” That is not how weighting works.


If an IA is worth 20%, scoring 75% of its raw marks contributes 15 percentage points to the final total:


0.75×20=150.75 \\times 20 = 15


0.75


×

The same raw percentage has a larger effect when the component carries more weight.


IA result IA weighting Weighted contribution


75% 20% 15 points


75% 25% 18.75 points


75% 30% 22.5 points


This is why advice about “how much the IA matters” must begin with the actual subject guide. Weightings vary, and assessment structures can change between syllabus versions. A general statement that every IA is worth the same amount is unreliable.


### Moderation can change the submitted mark


Maya's teacher may initially submit 15 out of 20, but that is not necessarily the mark used in the final calculation. The IB moderates internally assessed work to align marking standards across schools.


A sample representing the school's range of work is reviewed. If the IB judges that the teacher's marking was consistently generous or severe, marks for that component may be adjusted. They may rise, fall, or remain unchanged. The adjustment does not necessarily affect every student by an identical number of marks because moderation can vary across the mark range.


This is not a second judgment about whether Maya worked hard. It is a standardisation process. Two equally strong pieces of work should be treated comparably even when they were marked in different schools.


The practical lesson is to work closely from the published assessment criteria. Students can use RevisionDojo's Coursework Library to study how successful work is structured, while Grading tools can help identify criterion-specific weaknesses before submission. These resources should support original thinking, not replace it.


### How many marks does one IA point add?

For Maya's hypothetical component, worth 20% and marked out of 20, each raw mark contributes one point to the overall weighted total. If a different component were marked out of 24 but still worth 20%, each raw mark would contribute approximately:

That small calculation changes how a student interprets feedback. Moving from 14 to 16 out of 24 would add roughly 1.67 points to the weighted total, not two full percentage points.


The emotional impact of losing a raw mark is often larger than its mathematical impact. When students see the conversion clearly, they can replace vague panic with a concrete question: how many weighted points remain available elsewhere?


### How IB grade boundaries complete the picture


After the component marks are scaled and combined, the resulting total is compared with subject grade boundaries. These cut-offs separate grades 1-7. They are set for a particular subject, level, and examination session, so a boundary seen in one year should not be assumed to apply unchanged in another.


This explains why two students with similar IA marks can receive different final IB grades. Their examination marks may differ, they may study different levels, or their sessions may use different boundaries. The IA is one part of an aggregation process, not an independent grade guarantee.


For a deeper explanation, read[IB Grade Boundaries Explained for Parents](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-grade-boundaries-explained-parent-guide) or examine[how IB grade boundaries vary by year](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-grade-boundaries-by-year-what-a-7-requires) . Students comparing school forecasts with eventual results may also find the guide to[IB predicted grades versus final grades](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-predicted-grades-vs-final-grades) useful.


### What to do after receiving your IA mark


Maya cannot endlessly revise a submitted IA. She can, however, use the mark to build a sensible plan.


First, convert the raw result into a weighted contribution. Second, estimate what remains available across the examination components. Third, calculate several scenarios rather than relying on one perfect forecast.


Scenario Purpose


Conservative Shows the outcome if practice performance drops slightly


Current Uses a realistic average from recent timed work


Target Shows the marks needed to reach the desired boundary


Then preparation should follow the evidence. RevisionDojo's Questionbank helps students practise the topics costing them marks. Study Notes and Flashcards support recall, while AI Chat can clarify a difficult step without forcing students to search through unrelated material. Predicted Papers and Mock Exams are most useful later, when the goal shifts from understanding individual ideas to performing under timed conditions. Tutors can provide focused support when repeated practice reveals a persistent conceptual gap.


A weak IA calls for a stronger examination strategy, not resignation. A strong IA offers a cushion, not permission to stop. Students sometimes recover from a component that felt disastrous, a possibility explored in[how an imperfect paper or IA can still lead to a 7](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/mess-up-paper-ia-still-get-7) . The exact outcome always depends on the full weighted total and applicable boundaries.


### Turn the mark into a plan


By the time Maya closes the calculator, her IA mark has not changed. What has changed is its meaning. It is no longer a verdict hanging over the whole diploma. It is a known contribution within a larger calculation.


That is the healthiest way to read an IA result. Convert it accurately, allow for moderation, and focus on the marks still available.
